gaps.sentence: This bridge ___ repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Already' + present perfect passive: has been repaired.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

gaps.sentence: Your name ___ (find) anywhere on the guest list, I'm afraid.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive of ability/possibility: cannot be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
gaps.hint: continuing relevance from past to now
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

gaps.sentence: The finalists ___ (interview) live on air as we speak.
gaps.explanation: 'As we speak' demands the present continuous passive: are being + interviewed.

gaps.sentence: The matter ___ at this very moment, so no comment yet.
gaps.explanation: Look into (investigate) passivises with the particle kept: is being looked into.

gaps.sentence: Every complaint ___ (investigate) since the new ombudsman took over.
gaps.explanation: 'Every complaint' is singular, so present perfect passive: has been + investigated.
